mainTopic: The water-ditch partition, a person's ד׳ אמות on שבת, and joining courtyards with an עירוב
overview: The amud opens with the end of רבי חייא's teaching that a water ditch between two תחומין needs an iron partition, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא laughs at it. The גמרא tries several reasons for the laughter and rejects them one by one. It settles on the rule that חכמים were lenient with partitions for water, and supports this with רב's answer to רבי טבלא that a hanging partition works only for water. Next, on the משנה about a person asleep on the road at the start of שבת, רבא explains that חכמים give him eight by eight אמות for walking, while רבי יהודה gives four. For carrying, everyone agrees on four אמות. The גמרא then finds the source of the ד׳ אמות in the פסוק ״שבו איש תחתיו״: a body of three אמות plus one more. רב פפא rules that each person measures with his own forearm, except someone whose limbs are unusually small. Finally, the גמרא explains רבי שמעון's comparison to three courtyards and asks why the two outer courtyards are forbidden to each other. רב יהודה answers, and רב ששת begins a second answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ditch needs an iron partition to divide it
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי חייא's teaching: a ditch between two תחומין needs an iron partition to separate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: An iron partition is needed to divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last few words of רבי חייא's teaching from the previous lines. A ditch of water between two towns' שבת boundaries needs an iron partition to split it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the water in the ditch belongs to the תחום of each town and gets mixed together. Without a strong divider, people of one town would draw water that 'belongs' to the other town's area and carry it beyond its limit. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reacts to this teaching next, and the גמרא will try several explanations of what bothered him.

keyTerms.meaning: To divide it / cut it off
The שבת boundary (2000 אמות) beyond which one may not walk or carry objects

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The full teaching of רבי חייא is: 'A ditch between two תחומין needs an iron partition to divide it.' What the iron partition is supposed to do is not settled here. Later steps debate it: step 8 reads it as a real, working requirement, and step 9 suggests it may mean the ditch has no remedy at all. Step 10 then gives the final reason רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא laughed.

phrases.english: an iron partition to divide it.
phrases.notes: This is the end of רבי חייא's teaching about a ditch between two תחומין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא of רבי חייא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A water ditch lying between two תחומין must be divided by a partition as strong as iron, so that each town's water stays separate.

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא laughs at the teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא laughs at רבי חייא's teaching, treating it as unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי the son of רבי חנינא laughed at it.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא reacts to the teaching by laughing at it. This sets up the next question: why did he laugh?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laughing here is not just a mood. It is a quiet but strong rejection: he thinks no iron partition is needed at all. The גמרא will now try to work out what his reasoning was.

phrases.english: Laughed at it
phrases.notes: Shows he thought the ruling was unnecessary.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei the son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְחַיֵּיךְ עֲלֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A reaction to the teaching in step 1, which implies he disagrees with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא considers the iron-partition requirement unnecessary.

steps.title: Why did he laugh?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning was behind רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's laughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason he laughed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: what was his reason for laughing? This sets up the attempted answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laughter told us that he disagreed, but not why. The גמרא wants the actual legal reason behind his rejection.

phrases.english: What is the reason he laughs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the reaction in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal basis for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's dismissal of the iron-partition teaching.

steps.title: First suggestion: he holds like the lenient Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: Suggestion: רבי חייא taught strictly like רבי יוחנן בן נורי, while רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא holds leniently like רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because רבי חייא taught it strictly, like רבי יוחנן בן נורי, while רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא himself holds leniently, like the רבנן...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible reason. The two simply follow different sides of an older מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that ownerless things (חפצי הפקר) acquire שביתה, a 'home base' for שבת. On that view, the water in the ditch is tied to its spot, so a divider is needed. רבנן hold that ownerless things do not acquire שביתה, so no divider would be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: The word אילימא almost always signals that the suggestion coming next will be knocked down. Do not treat it as the final answer.

phrases.english: If you say it is because he taught it
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי חייא.

phrases.english: in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, stringently,
phrases.notes: His view is that ownerless things get their own Shabbos resting place (שביתה).

phrases.english: and he himself holds
phrases.notes: 'He himself' is רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

phrases.english: like the Rabbis, leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּתָנֵי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He laughed because he follows רבנן (ownerless items do not acquire שביתה), while the teaching follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

steps.title: You don't laugh at someone just for being stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion: holding a lenient view is no reason to mock someone who teaches a stricter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because he holds leniently, would he laugh at someone who teaches stringently?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first suggestion. A plain disagreement between two opinions does not explain laughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following one side of a real מחלוקת gives no grounds to ridicule someone who follows the other, legitimate side. Laughter suggests the teaching was clearly unnecessary even within its own framework. That points to a stronger reason.

phrases.english: And because he holds leniently,
does he laugh at one who teaches stringently?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question meaning 'surely not!'

steps.triggerLanguage: ומִשּׁוּם דְּסָבַר לְקוּלָּא מַאן דְּתָנֵי לְחוּמְרָא מְחַיֵּיךְ עֲלֵהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that the laughter came from following the other side of the רבי יוחנן בן נורי / רבנן dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A legitimate difference of opinion does not justify mocking the stricter view. Laughter requires the teaching to be clearly unnecessary.

steps.title: Second suggestion: flowing water is like the feet of everyone
steps.stepSummary: A second suggestion: a ברייתא teaches that flowing rivers and springs are 'like the feet of all people,' so the water never acquires a fixed home.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because a ברייתא teaches: flowing rivers and streaming springs are like the feet of all people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for the laughter, based on a ברייתא about flowing water. Even רבי יוחנן בן נורי would agree that moving water belongs to no fixed spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flowing water keeps moving, so it never 'settles' in one place to acquire שביתה. Whoever draws it may carry it wherever he himself may walk. If the ditch water is also flowing, the iron partition is pointless even for the strict view, and that is why he laughed.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the feet of every person: may be carried wherever the one who takes it may walk

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why one may use river or spring water on שבת without worrying where the water was before שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because it was taught in a baraita:
Flowing rivers and streaming springs —
they are like the feet of all people.
phrases.notes: The water acquires no שביתה of its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 5 with a new answer to the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He laughed because flowing water acquires no שביתה, so no partition is needed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: נהרות המושכין ומעיינות הנובעין הרי הן כרגלי כל אדם

steps.title: Maybe the ditch holds still, collected water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: perhaps רבי חייא's ditch holds collected, non-flowing water, so the ברייתא about flowing water does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is talking about collected water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second suggestion. Maybe the ditch in רבי חייא's teaching is still water, not flowing water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only covers moving water from rivers and springs. Still, collected water (מכונסין) sits in one place and can acquire שביתה, at least according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי. If that is the case here, the iron partition makes sense, and the laughter is still unexplained.
steps.confusionAlert: This rejection does not challenge the ברייתא itself. Flowing water is still 'like the feet of all people.' It only questions whether the ditch counts as flowing water.

phrases.english: But perhaps it deals with collected water.
phrases.notes: He means water that sits still in one place, not flowing rivers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the use of the ברייתא from step 6 by limiting the case of the ditch.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the application of the flowing-water ברייתא to רבי חייא's ditch, not the ברייתא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ditch may hold collected, still water, which can acquire שביתה, unlike flowing rivers and springs.

steps.title: A third reason: an iron partition is no better than reeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא laughed because רבי חייא required an iron מחיצה. Water passes through iron just as it passes through reeds, so the requirement seems pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he laughed because רבי חייא taught: 'It needs a partition of iron to separate it.' Why are reeds not good enough? Because water passes through them. But water passes through iron too!
steps.whatsHappening: Both earlier explanations were rejected, so the גמרא offers a new reason for the laughter. רבי חייא's ברייתא required an iron partition to divide the ditch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reeds are presumably rejected because water flows between them from one תחום to the other. Iron cannot be sealed perfectly either, so water still gets through. The iron requirement therefore seems to accomplish nothing, and that is what רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא found laughable.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous answer and offers a new one)
To divide it (to separate the ditch into two sections)

phrases.english: Rather, it is because he taught:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי חייא in his ברייתא.

phrases.english: 'It requires a partition of iron to divide it.'
phrases.notes: Quoting רבי חייא's ברייתא about the ditch between two תחומים.

phrases.english: And what is different about reeds, that they do not work?
phrases.notes: Here רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא starts explaining his thinking.

phrases.english: Because water enters through them,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל נָמֵי — עָיְילִי בְּהוּ מַיָּא.
phrases.english: With iron too, water enters through them!
phrases.notes: Iron cannot be sealed perfectly, so it has the same problem as reeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 undermined the ברייתא of flowing rivers, the גמרא offers a new explanation for the laughter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא laugh?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because requiring iron is pointless when water passes through iron just as it passes through reeds.

steps.title: Perhaps the ditch simply has no remedy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the iron-partition reason. Perhaps רבי חייא meant that the ditch would need an iron partition, which cannot work, so there is no fix at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he means: 'It would require an iron partition, and so there is no remedy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 8. It offers a different reading of רבי חייא's words that makes them perfectly sensible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 read רבי חייא as saying an iron partition is the solution. The גמרא now suggests he was saying the opposite. Only a perfect seal would help, and no such seal is possible, so the ditch's water simply cannot be used. On this reading the ruling is strict but logical, and there is nothing to laugh at.

keyTerms.meaning: And it has no remedy (there is no fix)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'צריך מחיצה של ברזל' as practical advice to build an iron wall. In this reading it means 'only an impossible iron wall would help', which is a way of saying it can't be fixed.

phrases.english: But perhaps he is saying: 'It requires (iron), and there is no remedy.'
phrases.notes: He mentions iron only to show it can't be done, so there's really no fix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8 by rereading רבי חייא's words.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the iron-partition explanation for the laughter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed רבי חייא offered iron as a working solution. He may have meant there is no solution at all.

steps.title: The real reason: the Sages were lenient with water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's final explanation is that חכמים were lenient with partitions for water. Even a minimal partition works, so a ruling that demands iron or declares 'no remedy' is laughable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a leniency that the Sages were lenient regarding water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new and final reason for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's laughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For water, חכמים accepted even a weak or symbolic partition as enough to separate the areas. So requiring iron, or ruling that the ditch can't be fixed, goes against this known leniency. That is why רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא laughed.
steps.whatToRemember: Final reason for the laughter: חכמים were lenient with partitions for water, so a minimal partition is enough and iron is unnecessary.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle (קל הוא שהקילו חכמים במים) is a known rule in הלכות עירובין and comes up again wherever partitions over water are discussed.

phrases.english: Because it is a leniency
phrases.notes: Read this as: he laughed because...

phrases.english: that the Sages were lenient regarding water.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקַל הוּא שֶׁהֵקֵילּוּ חֲכָמִים בְּמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 rejected the iron explanation, this offers the final reason for the laughter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא laugh?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because חכמים were lenient with partitions for water, so demanding iron is unjustified.

steps.title: Setting up support from רבי טבלא's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the water leniency to the case of רבי טבלא. He asked רב whether a hanging partition permits carrying in a ruin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of רבי טבלא, for רבי טבלא asked רב: Does a hanging partition permit carrying in a ruin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up support for the leniency with water by bringing a related story. Here it only states רבי טבלא's question, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחיצה תלויה is a wall that hangs in the air and does not reach the ground. רבי טבלא asked whether such a wall makes a ruined building count as an enclosed area. The point the גמרא is building toward is that such a hanging partition works only for water, which shows the water leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the case of רבי טבלא
A hanging partition (does not reach the ground)

phrases.english: Like the case of Rabbi Tavla,
for Rabbi Tavla asked Rav:
A hanging partition, does it permit carrying in a ruin?
phrases.notes: Do the hanging remains of walls count as if they reach the ground?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבִּי טַבְלָא, דִּבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי טַבְלָא מֵרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins bringing a source to support step 10's principle that חכמים were lenient with water.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that חכמים were lenient with partitions for water.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי טבלא's question to רב about a מחיצה תלויה in a ruin (the answer continues next).

steps.title: רב answers that a hanging partition works only for water
steps.stepSummary: רב answers רבי טבלא: a hanging partition does not permit carrying in a ruin. It works only for water, because חכמים were lenient with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: A hanging partition permits only in the case of water. It is a special leniency that חכמים made for water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question רבי טבלא asked in the previous step. The answer is no: a hanging partition does not help for a ruin, only for water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hanging partition does not reach the ground, so normally it is not a real wall. רב says חכמים accepted it only for water. This is exactly the proof the גמרא needed from step 10: for water, חכמים accept even a weak partition, so demanding an iron wall makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: A hanging partition, a wall that does not reach the ground
It is a leniency that חכמים made for water

steps.whatToRemember: For water, חכמים accepted even a weak partition, such as a hanging one. That is why a ruling that requires an iron partition for a water ditch seemed laughable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the proof for step 10. The idea that 'חכמים were lenient with water' is now backed by a real ruling from רב.

phrases.english: He (Rav) said to him (Rabbi Tavla):
A hanging partition does not permit
except in the case of water,
it is a leniency that the Sages were lenient with water.
phrases.notes: This is the source for the idea that water partitions are treated leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין מְחִיצָה תְּלוּיָה מַתֶּרֶת אֶלָּא בְּמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי טבלא's question from step 11, and in doing so completes the proof for step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a hanging partition permit carrying in a ruin?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. A hanging partition works only for water, as a special leniency of חכמים.

steps.title: The opinions of חכמים and רבי יהודה seem identical
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: חכמים say he has only four אמות. It then asks how רבי יהודה differs, since he also says four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And חכמים say he has only four אמות, etc.' But רבי יהודה's view seems to be the same as the first תנא's view!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about someone who fell asleep on the road before שבת began. It asks what the argument is, because both opinions seem to say 'four אמות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים say the sleeper gets four אמות. רבי יהודה says he gets four אמות in whatever direction he wants. On the surface both give four אמות, so it is unclear why the משנה presents two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Four אמות (cubits), the small area a person always has around him on שבת
The first תנא, the first opinion in the משנה (here, חכמים)
Etc.; the rest of the quote continues in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'תנא קמא' means חכמים, whose view is quoted just before רבי יהודה's. It does not mean רבי יוחנן בן נורי, whose view appears earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: "And the Sages say:
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה.

phrases.english: he has only four (cubits), etc."
Rabbi Yehuda is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the water-partition discussion and begins a new line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's presentation of רבי יהודה as a separate opinion from חכמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions give four אמות, so there seems to be no real disagreement.

steps.title: רבא: the difference is an eight-by-eight area
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that they disagree about an area of eight by eight אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The difference between them is an area of eight by eight אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by showing the real difference between חכמים and רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים mean four אמות in every direction from where the person stands. That adds up to a square of eight by eight. רבי יהודה gives only four אמות total, in one direction the person chooses.

keyTerms.meaning: Eight by eight (אמות), a square area
There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read חכמים' 'four אמות' as a total of four. It means four in each direction, which is why their area is bigger than רבי יהודה's.

phrases.english: Rava said:
(An area of) eight by eight (cubits)
is (the difference) between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמוֹנֶה עַל שְׁמוֹנֶה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the four אמות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both opinions give the same four אמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים give four אמות in every direction (eight by eight). רבי יהודה gives four אמות in one chosen direction.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the eight-by-eight reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא openly states that the person has eight by eight אמות, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: He has eight by eight אמות. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says outright what רבא explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the eight-by-eight area in the name of רבי מאיר. The unnamed חכמים of the משנה are therefore רבי מאיר. This confirms that their view is a larger area than רבי יהודה's four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא), a phrase introducing support

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a baraita):
He has eight by eight (cubits),
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's explanation that חכמים allow eight by eight.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating 'he has eight by eight, the words of רבי מאיר'.

steps.title: The argument is only about walking, not carrying
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the argument to walking. For carrying, everyone agrees: four אמות yes, more than that no.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The argument is about walking. But for carrying, everyone agrees: four אמות is allowed, more than that is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new rule that limits where the argument he just explained applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eight-by-eight area of חכמים applies only to how far the person may walk. Even according to חכמים, he may carry an object only four אמות. Carrying it farther is forbidden by all opinions.
steps.whatToRemember: חכמים: walk within eight by eight. רבי יהודה: four אמות in one chosen direction. For carrying, everyone agrees on only four אמות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that permission to walk an area and permission to carry objects across it are measured separately.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The dispute is regarding walking,
but regarding carrying, all agree:
four cubits, yes,
more (than that), no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the eight-by-eight dispute so it applies only to walking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute concerns walking only. For carrying, all agree the limit is four אמות.

steps.title: Where do the four אמות come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the תורה source of the ד׳ אמות that every person always has on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these four אמות, where are they written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has been using the idea that a person always has ד׳ אמות. Now it stops and asks where this idea is hinted at in the Torah. This step sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now everyone took the ד׳ אמות for granted, both for walking and for carrying. The גמרא wants to know what the number is based on. It is a request for a source, not an attack on the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits: the small personal space a person always has on שבת
Where is it written? A request for a תורה source

phrases.english: And these four cubits
where are they written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 16 used the ד׳ אמות as a fixed rule. This step asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The תורה basis for the rule that a person always has ד׳ אמות on שבת.

steps.title: A person's place is his body plus one cubit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns the ד׳ אמות from ״שבו איש תחתיו״. A body is three אמות, and one more אמה is added. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה give different reasons for that extra אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: ״Remain every man in his place״ means a space like his place. And how big is his place? His body is three אמות, plus one אמה so he can stretch out his hands and feet. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: his body is three אמות, plus one אמה so he can pick up an object from under his feet and put it under his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The פסוק ״שבו איש תחתיו״ tells a person to stay in 'his place', and his place is the space his body takes up plus a little extra, which adds up to four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״תחתיו״ is read as ״כתחתיו״, meaning an area the size of the space a person fills. Both תנאים agree on three אמות for the body plus one more. They disagree only about why the extra אמה is needed: רבי מאיר says it is for stretching out, and רבי יהודה says it is for moving an object from his feet to his head.

keyTerms.meaning: Remain every man in his place (שמות ט״ז:כ״ט)
Like his place: an area the size of the space he fills
To stretch out his hands and feet

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree here about whether it is four אמות. Both say three plus one. They only disagree about what the extra אמה is for, and the next steps show why that matters.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"Remain every man in his place"
means an area like his place.
And how much is his place?
His body is three cubits,
and one cubit so he can stretch out his hands and feet
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: גּוּפוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: His body is three cubits,
and one cubit so that he can pick up an object
from under his feet
and put it down under his head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 with a ברייתא and a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ד׳ אמות come from ״שבו איש תחתיו״: a body of three אמות plus one extra אמה. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה give different reasons for the extra אמה.

steps.title: What is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the reasons of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: Both תנאים ended up with four אמות, so the גמרא asks whether their different reasons change anything in practice. This step sets up the answer that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both opinions give the same four אמות, the argument looks like it is only about the reason. The גמרא is looking for a real case where the two reasons give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? A request for the practical result of an argument

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical meaning of the argument in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between רבי מאיר's reason and רבי יהודה's reason for the extra אמה.

steps.title: Exactly four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether the space is exactly four אמות. According to רבי יהודה it is exactly four. According to רבי מאיר, stretching out hands and feet gives a little more.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: exactly four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument changes the actual size of the space. רבי יהודה gives exactly four אמות, while רבי מאיר gives a little more than four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's extra אמה is for moving an object from feet to head, which fits inside exactly four אמות. רבי מאיר's extra אמה is for stretching out hands and feet, and that reaches a bit past four. So רבי יהודה measures 'tight' and רבי מאיר measures 'roomy'.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Exact, tight: no extra space added

steps.whatToRemember: The ד׳ אמות come from ״שבו איש תחתיו״: a body of three אמות plus one. For רבי יהודה it is exactly four. For רבי מאיר it is a bit more, because a person can stretch out.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
exactly four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה gives exactly four אמות. רבי מאיר gives slightly roomier אמות, enough to stretch out hands and feet.

steps.title: Whose cubit measures the four cubits?
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא tells his son to ask רב פפא whether the ד׳ אמות are measured with each person's own forearm or with the standard אמה used for הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said to his son: When you go in to רב פפא, ask him: The four אמות that the Rabbis spoke about, do we give them to a person measured with his own אמה, or measured with the אמה of הקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question comes up about how to measure the ד׳ אמות. Is it measured with each person's own arm, or with one standard measure that applies to everyone? This step sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The space is based on a person's own body, so maybe his own forearm should be the ruler, and a tall man would get more than a short man. On the other hand, maybe the Rabbis used one fixed measure, the standard אמה used for הקדש, for everyone. The question is about how to carry out the rule, not about the rule itself.

keyTerms.meaning: With his own cubit: measured by the person's own forearm
The standard cubit used for consecrated matters

steps.confusionAlert: The word ״אמה״ means both 'forearm' and 'cubit'. That double meaning is the whole question: is the 'cubit' this person's actual forearm, or a standard unit?

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said to his son:
When you go in before Rav Pappa,
ask him:
The four cubits that they spoke about,
do we give them to him measured with his own cubit,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בְּאַמָּה שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ יָהֲבִינַן לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: or do we give them to him measured with the cubit of the Sanctuary?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לִבְרֵיהּ כִּי עָיְילַתְּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא בְּעִי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the size of the ד׳ אמות is set, this step asks which unit of measure to use.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether each person's ד׳ אמות are measured by his own forearm or by the standard אמה of הקדש.

steps.title: A two-sided trap: עוג's size or the missing list entry
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא prepares his son for either answer רב פפא might give. Each possible answer meets its own difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he tells you we give the person cubits of the holy (standard) size, then what about עוג מלך הבשן? And if he tells you we give the person cubits by his own forearm, ask him: why isn't this rule taught together with the list 'There are things where they said everything goes according to the person'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא is still talking to his son. He gives him a challenge for each answer רב פפא might give to the question about how to measure the ד׳ אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one is the standard אמה of קדש. That cannot work for a giant like עוג, whose body would not even fit in four standard אמות. Option two is each person's own forearm. Then the rule should appear in the משנה that lists measures that depend on the person, and it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: the fixed, standard אמה used for the בית המקדש and הקדש
עוג, the giant king of הבשן

keyTerms.term: יֵשׁ שֶׁאָמְרוּ הַכֹּל לְפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם
keyTerms.meaning: the משנה listing measures that change according to each person

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב משרשיא is asking two separate questions. It is one trap with two sides: whichever answer רב פפא picks, a difficulty is waiting.

phrases.english: If he says to you:
We give him cubits of the holy (standard) size

phrases.aramaic: עוֹג מֶלֶךְ הַבָּשָׁן מַה תְּהֵא עָלָיו?
phrases.english: then Og king of Bashan, what will be with him?
phrases.notes: His body was far bigger than four standard cubits.

phrases.english: And if he says to you
we give him cubits by his own forearm,
say to him:
Why is it not taught
together with 'There are things where they said'
'everything goes according to the person'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמַר לָךְ: אַמּוֹת שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ יָהֲבִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the planned challenges to the question from step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: Both possible ways of measuring the ד׳ אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The standard אמה fails for a giant. The personal אמה should then be listed in the משנה of measures that depend on the person, but it is not.

steps.title: רב פפא pushes back on too much precision
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that examining every detail this closely would stop all learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came before רב פפא, רב פפא said to him: If we were this exact about everything, we would never get to learn anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The son brings the question to רב פפא. רב פפא first objects to how picky the challenge is, and this sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא is not denying the difficulty. He is saying that not every missing item in a list is a real problem. Even so, he goes on to give an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: we would not get to learn

phrases.english: When he came before Rav Pappa,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי דָּיְיקִינַן כּוּלֵּא הַאי,
phrases.english: he said to him: If we were this exact about everything,
we would never get to learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דָּיְיקִינַן כּוּלֵּא הַאי, לָא הֲוֵי תָּנֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First reaction to the challenge in step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The overall demand that every rule be included in every list
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Reading the lists this precisely is unreasonable.

steps.title: Use your own forearm, but the rule has exceptions
steps.stepSummary: Each person uses his own אמה. The rule is left out of the 'depends on the person' list because it does not always apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, we give each person cubits by his own forearm. As for what bothered you, why it isn't listed with 'There are things they said': it is not a clear-cut rule, because there can be a person whose limbs are unusually small.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his real answer. He picks the personal-forearm option and explains why the משנה's list leaves it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of 'everything according to the person' holds only rules that apply without exception. Here there is an exception: a ננס באבריו, whose arms are small compared to his body. He gets the standard אמה of קדש instead, so the rule was not included in that list.

keyTerms.meaning: really / in truth (keeping the original position)
someone whose limbs are small compared to his body

steps.whatToRemember: The ד׳ אמות are measured with each person's own forearm. The exception is someone with unusually short limbs, who gets the standard אמה. Because of that exception, the rule is not in the list of 'according to the person' measures.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a list in the משנה may include only rules that apply with no exceptions.

phrases.english: Really, we give him cubits by his own forearm.
And as for what bothers you:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא קָתָנֵי גַּבֵּי ״יֵשׁ שֶׁאָמְרוּ״?
phrases.english: why is it not taught with 'There are things they said'?
Because it is not clear-cut,
since there can be someone whose limbs are unusually small.
phrases.notes: Such a person is measured by the standard cubit instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real answer after the push-back in step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side and explains why the list leaves it out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the personal forearm is used, the משנה's list should have included it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list includes only rules with no exceptions. This rule has the exception of a person with unusually short limbs.

steps.title: Why did רבי שמעון need a comparison?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about two people whose ד׳ אמות overlap. It asks why רבי שמעון added 'To what is this similar?'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If there were two people, and part of one person's cubits overlapped the other's, etc.' Why did רבי שמעון need to say 'To what is this similar?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה and opens a new question. This sets up an explanation of why רבי שמעון compared this case to three courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, two people whose areas overlap may eat together in the shared middle area. רבי שמעון compares this to three courtyards that open into each other. The גמרא wants to know what this comparison adds that the plain rule did not already say.

keyTerms.meaning: part of his cubits (his ד׳ אמות area)
to what is this similar (a comparison formula)
why does he need to say
etc. (the quote of the משנה continues)

phrases.english: If there were two
and part of the cubits of this one, etc.
Why does he need to say
'To what is this similar?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי שמעון's comparison to three courtyards adds to the rule

steps.title: רבי שמעון's comparison is a challenge to the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says to the רבנן: the overlapping ד׳ אמות case is just like the three-courtyard case. So why do you argue with me there and not here?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי שמעון was saying to the רבנן: After all, what is this case like? It is like three courtyards that open into each other and also open into a public area. What is different there, that you argue with me, and what is different here, that you do not argue with me?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from step 25. It explains that 'To what is this similar?' was not just a comparison. It was רבי שמעון's argument against the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ד׳ אמות case, everyone agrees: the middle person may carry with each outer person, but the two outer people may not carry with each other. רבי שמעון points out that the three-courtyard case has the same structure, yet there the רבנן argue with him. He wants them to explain why they treat the two cases differently.

keyTerms.meaning: After all; since it is so (opens a logical argument)

steps.whyThisMatters: It changes how we read רבי שמעון's words in the משנה. They are not a side illustration. They are an argument meant to win over the רבנן on the courtyard case.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Shimon was saying to the Rabbis:
After all, to what is this matter similar?
To three courtyards that open into one another,
and that also open into the public domain.
What is different there, that you disagree with me,
phrases.notes: In the courtyard case the רבנן do not accept רבי שמעון's lenient view.

phrases.english: and what is different here, that you do not disagree?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case of overlapping ד׳ אמות.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 about why רבי שמעון added 'To what is this similar?'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי שמעון added the comparison to three courtyards.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a challenge to the רבנן: they should rule the same way in both cases.

steps.title: The Rabbis answer: courtyards have many residents
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reply that courtyards have many residents, so mistakes are likely. Here there are only three people, so mistakes are unlikely.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? There, the residents are many. Here, the residents are not many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer to רבי שמעון's challenge. They explain why the two cases are not really the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With many residents in the courtyards, someone could easily carry between the two outer courtyards by mistake. So the רבנן forbid all three courtyards to each other. With only three people, they can easily remind each other, so the רבנן did not need to make an extra rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The two cases follow the same basic logic. The רבנן are only stricter with courtyards because many residents make mistakes more likely.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis (how do they answer)?
There (in the courtyards), the residents are numerous.
Here (in the ד׳ אמות case), the residents are not numerous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the רבנן against רבי שמעון's challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The courtyard case and the ד׳ אמות case are the same, so the רבנן are inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The courtyards have many residents, so mistakes are likely and the רבנן are stricter. Three people can remind each other.

steps.title: Why are the two outer courtyards forbidden to each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the two outer courtyards are forbidden to each other. It asks why, since both joined with the middle one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the two outer ones, etc.' And why? Since the outer courtyards made an עירוב with the middle one, they should all count as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line of the משנה about three courtyards and challenges it. It asks why the two outer courtyards may not carry to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both outer courtyards made an עירוב with the middle courtyard. It seems logical that this links all three into one unit. If so, the two outer courtyards should also be allowed to carry to each other.

phrases.english: The משנה taught: 'And the two outer ones, etc.'
phrases.notes: The full line: the two outer ones are forbidden to each other.

phrases.english: And why (are they forbidden)?

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּעָרְבִי לְהוּ חִיצוֹנוֹת בַּהֲדֵי אֶמְצָעִית,
phrases.english: Since the outer ones made an עירוב with the middle one,
they all become one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line in the משנה about the three courtyards and challenges its ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the two outer courtyards are forbidden to each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Joining both outer courtyards with the middle one should merge all three into one unit, which would permit carrying between the outer two.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the middle courtyard placed its עירוב in each outer one
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the משנה's case is one where the middle courtyard put one עירוב in each outer courtyard. So the outer two were never joined together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The case is where the middle courtyard placed its עירוב in this courtyard and its עירוב in that courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the challenge by defining the exact case in the משנה. This explains why the outer courtyards stay forbidden to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both outer courtyards had put their עירוב food in the middle courtyard, all the food would sit in one place, and all three would become one. Here, the middle courtyard made two separate עירובין, one in each outer courtyard. Each outer courtyard is linked only to the middle one, never to the other outer one.

keyTerms.meaning: Shared food that joins courtyards so residents may carry between them on שבת
For example; the case is where

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the outer courtyards stay forbidden just because they are far apart. The reason is where the עירוב food was placed. There are two separate joinings, not one shared one.
steps.whatToRemember: The two outer courtyards are forbidden to each other only when the middle courtyard placed separate עירובין in each of them. Then the outer two never share one עירוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
The case is where the middle courtyard placed
its עירוב in this (outer) one and its עירוב in that (outer) one.
phrases.notes: So the food of the two outer courtyards is never together in one place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּתְנָה אֶמְצָעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outer courtyards joined with the middle one in one shared עירוב, so all three should be one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The middle courtyard made two separate עירובין, one in each outer courtyard. The outer two were never joined, so they stay forbidden to each other.

steps.title: רב ששת's alternative answer: even with the עירוב in the middle courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers the question differently from רב יהודה. Even if the outer courtyards put their עירוב in the middle courtyard, the outer two can still be forbidden to each other. It depends on the specific way the food was placed. The details of that case continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: You can even say that the outer courtyards put their עירוב in the middle courtyard. Still, we are dealing with a case where they placed it in a particular way. (The sentence continues on the next amud.)
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins a second answer to the question of why the two outer courtyards are forbidden to each other. He keeps the simple picture, with the food in the middle courtyard, and starts to describe a special case that still keeps the outer two apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה needed the food to be in the outer courtyards so that the outer two never shared one place. רב ששת says that change is not needed. Even with the food in the middle courtyard, the outer two stay apart if the food was placed in a certain way. The words 'כגון שנתנוהו' open that special case, and the next amud finishes it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Even if you say'. It means 'I can accept the harder version of the case and still answer'
Their עירוב: the shared food that joins courtyards so carrying between them is allowed on שבת
'For example' or 'in a case where'. It introduces the specific case being described

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב ששת agrees with רב יהודה. רב יהודה said the food was in the outer courtyards. רב ששת says that even if the food was in the middle courtyard, the outer two can still be forbidden to each other. These are two different ways of explaining the משנה.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.english: Even if you say that they placed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second answer to the same question from step 28, offered instead of רב יהודה's answer in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the specific case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about a special way of placing the עירוב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the outer courtyards placed their food in the middle courtyard, it seems all three should count as one joined area, so the outer two should be allowed to each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with the food in the middle courtyard, the specific way it was placed keeps the two outer courtyards from joining each other. The details continue in the next section.
